Hello! New to the area? Moving here soon? Well ask your questions and get some answers. Where should you live, eat, play, shop? These were all commonly asked questions in the sub on the website of the Great Satan. So I figured I would nip it in the bud early and make a thread for new and soon to be transplants to ask questions and get locals answers but also as an locals encyclopedia for the categories mentioned above and more. Please Ask, Add ,and Share as you see fit. Cheers and welcome to town.
New/Moving to Reno? This is the thread for you.
Eat Catagory. Restaurants, groceries, even fast food. Questions and answers on these can be posted to here.

This was a reply to /u/jennyrokus' new to town question and what inspired this thread. Regarding Local Restaurants. Slightly edited.

So I'll break the list down into categories, many will have crossover so the same names might be in several categories. Breakfast: All locals love Peg's. It's popular and the food is good but I honestly think PJ's on Wells Ave has better breakfast food and you can get a Bloody Mary there. Also good breakfast (and lunch) down that way is Cafe Deluxe. For weekend brunch hit up Old Granite St Eatery or Creme. All offer fairly standard breakfast brunch fair, Peg's or PJ's offer more classics (Eggs Benedict, French Toast, Etc.) Cafe Deluxe has many Vegetarian/vegan choices, Granite St., and Creme have more haute brunch fare

Lunch: Sup, Midtown Eats, Granite St., Campo, Greatful Gardens, Cafe Deluxe. Granite and Campo I feel are better for business lunches or a leisurely day. Midtown and Granite St. offer New American, higher end sandwiches,salads and table service. Sup (pronounced Soup) has all house-made soups,salads and sandwiches,order at the counter but a server brings out your food. Campo is high end yet simple Italian, has more American offerings at lunch (sandwich, burgers,etc) Deluxe and Grateful offer lighter and more veg/vegan options.

Casual to mid-level dinner: Campo, Granite St., Midtown Eats, The Gas Lamp, Pignic Pub and Patio, Bangkok Cuisine, Thai Chili, Reef Sushi, Sushi Lover, Noble Pie and JJ's Pie. Yes a lot of repeats here so just think the above descriptions but dinner, full courses, etc. The Gas Lamp would be on par with the aforementioned but only do dinner. Pignic is fun, you grill your own stuff, bring it or buy it there. Bangkok and Thai are obvious but again locals all say Bangkok but I like Thai Chili better. Reef Sushi/Sushi Lover, obvious but there are a lot of choices there and I don't want to kick off the great Reno Sushi debate of 2015, suffice to say they're both really good. Noble Pie/JJ's Pie, good local pizza.

Fine Dining: 4th St Bistro, Beaujolais Bistro, LuLou's, La Famiglia. All are fine dining, formal atmospheres. 4th St and LuLou's have the most haute cuisine in town. Personally, and most would agree 4th St is the best. Beaujolais is formal French fare, La Famiglia formal Italian.
Drink and be merry. Bars, booze and nightclubs. Find the best hangouts, locally made brews and spirits, and dance floors here. Also Music scenes, movies and local events.
Play. Parks, hiking, camping, skiing, biking, and all things outdoors.
Live. Where to live, where not to. Find the places to live for the college aged, young professionals, families, and more here.

The only areas I would drive through but not live in are East Neal Road, past the Atlantis and south/north Wells Ave and Mill area (around Renown Hospital) and North Wells around the Livestock Event Center. These are the only places I've ever seen RPD Gang Units and once a mugging. Again I would drive through these areas day or night, maybe making sure doors are locked. I have a lot of odd phobias so I lock my car doors at night no matter where i am. I would however avoid living in these areas.

Yes 4th St., has a ton of homeless and crackheads but they're mostly harmless. I wouldn't walk alone at night very far, especially impaired and espically further East. But the homeless shelter and bus station are on E 4th so what do you expect and most of the weekly motels line west 4th, so for most people living on 4th isn't an issue as there aren't many conventional apartments or houses, but you may have to pass through it from time to time.

That's my personal where not to live list. If anyone disagrees or has something to add please do.

Where to live. I'm going to stick to areas I have lived over the years and leave other spots to those who live there or have. Mid-town. This area has progressed the most over the years. Tons of local businesses and a youthful population. You can find a mix of hipsters and young professionals here. This place has had a major face lift and some of the older more gritty elements remain. Consequently rents have gone up but there are still affordable area's for the young professionals and roommate situations.

UNR/University Terrace/ Kings Row. So obviously this is student central. Campus housing around the school. A mix of mostly rental houses and small apartment buildings in the University Terrace/Ralston St area closer to campus. Lots of college kids renting houses with a smattering of middle-aged and older renters and owners. Few school aged kids. More young to middle aged home owners in the University Terrace area closer to keystone Ave. Kings row is a good mix of Owners and Renters. Many College aged people as well as young families and starter homes. Roomie situations galore. A small but significant amount of retiree aged home owners.

W.2nd St/Dickerson Rd. This is what I like to call a budget area. Now it's in close proximity to 4th st. so many times there are crack heads out and about, sometimes more than others. This doesn't personally bother me and I never once had an issue, no break-in's, thefts or muggings. But it is also close to really nice area's like Mayberry and California Ave. Further down on Dickerson you have many nicer, newer townhouses in gated communities for far less rent or sale for far cheaper than other areas. Dickerson also dead ends into the beautiful Oxbow Park. Up on west 2nd there are some very nice and middle of the road older apartments that still have affordable rent. The area is still a bit gritty but i think as the market rebounds it has the potential to become a rival to midtown.
Shop. Fashion needs and niche item stores can be found here.

OK, its getting late but I want to post in as many categories as possible before hitting the hay and this one will be one of the easiest and shortest for me. I am probably one of the least fashionable gay men in existence. I'm in my 30's and married and like many straight guys at my age/marital status trips to the mall are like passing through the 7th circle. That said there are two main malls in Reno and an outlet mall in Sparks. For those who don't know Sparks is the city that directly borders Reno to the East. Think of us like a podunk Minneapolis-St.Paul but with blackjack and hookers!

So, Meadow Wood Mall and The Summit are the conventional malls, Legends is in Sparks but just off 80-E is the outlet mall. Meadow Wood is south of downtown and The Summit is at the far south end of Reno in the Galenia area. Meadow Wood is indoors the Summit outdoors, The former has Macy's the latter has Dillard's. The outlet mall has your standards at cheaper prices. It's newer so the shops are nice and more well maintained than some other outlet nightmares plus a giant Scheels is there for all your outdoor sporting needs(see play category for more). That does it for my mall knowledge. Please someone more with it fashionably chime in.

The main local 2nd hand stores off the top of my head are Junkee's and Plato's Closet, both in mid-town. We have your standard Salvation Army and Savers too.

For anything and everything hippy or Burning Man find it at the Melting Pot in mid-town. Need incense? They have it. Pipe, vaporizer, grinder? gotcha covered. That perfect feather boa and fur boot combo for the Playa, you bet! I personally share the opinions of Eric Cartman when it comes to this category but I'll reserve my tirade for a more appropriate thread. But of that's your thing this is probably one of the best places for it and at least it's locally owned!
